docs.text: BillCore encapsulates searches ( SearchByID ), memo storage ( PutItemMemo / GetItemMemo ), amount tables ( BillAmountTbl ) and EDI flags ( BillTbl::Rec ). Documents coordinate: EDI/Flags → amount lookups → posting/stock movements → status updates (posted, archived, canceled). File references such as CheckAmtTypeRef , GetAmountList , CalcBillLineAmount define invariants that Surypus must encode with LiquidHaskell. Документ bill.cpp также содержит методы BillCore::GetAmount , GetAmountList , GetQttyEpsilon , SetRecadvStatus / SetRecadvConfStatus — эти методы задают инварианты остатков, документов и статусов, которые нужно отразить в LiquidHaskell. При публикации документа BillCore::Post (далее в файле) вызывает CalcBillLineAmount , GetAmountList , CheckAmtTypeRef , GetQttyEpsilon и затем направляет накопленные суммы в AccTurn / Stock — Surypus должен сохранить эту последовательность через Hasql + SQL-процедуры.

docs.text: Пользователь создаёт или обновляет BillTbl::Rec , заполняя Flags2 (EDI, статус) и строки ( BillLineTbl ). BillCore::BillCore / BillCore::UpdateStatus проверяют и модифицируют флаги перед сохранением. BillCore::GetAmountList и AmtEntry строят список сумм по типам ( AmtTypeID ), который затем используется BillCore::CheckAmtTypeRef / BillCore::SelectAmountType при постинге: суммы должны совпадать с сформированными проводками. При постинге BillCore::Post : - вычисляет lineAmount через CalcBillLineAmount (чистая логика: qty*price – discount + tax), - вызывает MakeOrder , AccTurn , Stock / Lot для отражения движения товаров и бухгалтерии, - обновляет BillTbl::Flags2 (статусы: BILLF2_POSTED , BILLF2_EDI_* ). BillCore::SetRecadvStatus , SetRecadvConfStatus устанавливают флаги EDI-статусов (принят/отклонён/промежуточный). Surypus должен иметь типы BillEdiStatus / BillEdiConfStatus с теми же значениями и функции, поддерживающие Flags2 в BillLine . BillCore::GetQttyEpsilon возвращает значение точности для проверок остатков; Surypus должен хранить это значение в конфиге и использовать в LiquidHaskell-выражениях (например, qtty_eps при сопоставлении остатков лотов).

docs.text: Документальный модуль Surypus 1. Что делает оригинальная реализация PPObjRegister и PPObjRegisterType описывают регистры документов, их типы и флаги REGTF_* ( UNIQUE , DUPNUMBER , ONLYNUMBER , LOCATION , WARNEXPIRY и др.). Регистры называются по номеру Num , привязаны к объектам ( PPOBJ_PERSON / PPOBJ_LOCATION ) и, при необходимости, требуют уникальности номера ( CheckUniqueNumber ), учитывают тип объекта и предупреждают об истечении срока ( REGTF_WARNEXPIRY ). При создании регистра ( PPObjRegister::HandleMsg , Helper_EditDialog ) система подбирает RegType , автоматически вычисляет даты ( ExpiryPeriod ), переводит пользователя на ввод только номера ( REGTF_ONLYNUMBER ) и запрещает дублирование номеров по типу, если у типа нет REGTF_DUPNUMBER . Номера регистров получают из хранимой процедуры document_get_next_register_number ( config/schema_Core_Document_Register.sql ), а проверки концентрации выполняются функцией document_register_number_exists . Отдельно существует счётчик документов ( document_op_counter / document_get_next_doc_number ) для операций ( objregt.cpp и config/schema_Core_Document_OpCounter.sql ), которые формируют номера документов через префикс и флаг REGTF_DUPNUMBER . 2. Как это отражено в Surypus Core.Document.Types теперь экспортирует DocumentRegisterFlag и вспомогательные предикаты ( documentRegisterTypeAllowsDuplicateNumbers , documentRegisterTypeOnlyNumber , documentRegisterTypeForLocation и др.), которые соответствуют REGTF_* и позволяют верифицировать бизнес-инварианты на уровне LiquidHaskell. DB.Document.Register загружает тип ( DB.Document.RegisterType.getRegisterType ) и запускает checkDuplicate , который использует новые предикаты, чтобы повторно применять условие REGTF_DUPNUMBER из C++. DB.Document.RegisterType и DB.Document.Counter продолжают хранить размеры (код, флаги, префиксы), а API в APIServer.documentRoutes предоставляет CRUD + генерацию следующего номера, как в интерфейсах PPObjRegisterType . SQL-модули ( config/schema_Core_Document_* ) отделяют Core.Document и PPObjRegister , и docs/engineering/schema-uniqueness.md содержит описание, почему коллизии AccSheet / OpCounter разобраны. 3. Потоки данных, сохранённые в Surypus Создание регистра: контролируется validateDocumentRegister , resolveNumber , documentRegisterTypeAllowsDuplicateNumbers . Номер документа: при drAutoNumber вызывается document_get_next_register_number , потом checkDuplicate проверяет, не нарушает ли флаг REGTF_DUPNUMBER . Тип документа: documentOpCounter сгенерирует номер через document_get_next_doc_number , в APIServer уже есть endpoint /documents/counters/:id/next-number . 4. Следующие шаги, чтобы завершить портирование Подключить флаги REGTF_WARNEXPIRY / REGTF_WARNABSENCE к API и Domain, чтобы при запросе регистра фронтенд мог подсветить статус (например в QML показать “истекает/нет” по documentRegisterStatusAsOf ). Расширить job-сервер Surypus/Surypus/JobRunner.hs , чтобы асинхронно запускать document_register_audit (новая задача), которая проверяет немедленно истекающие регистры и повторяющиеся номера на стороне PostgreSQL ( DB.Document.Audit ). Добавить новый REST-некрон /api/v1/documents/audit , который создает джоб document_register_audit с любым lookaheadDays (по умолчанию 30), чтобы UI/ETL могли запускать аудит по расписанию или при импорте данных. Перенести CrystalReports (структуры document_register , document_op_counter ) в Jasper/Pentaho/Helical, чтобы отчёты ссылались на те же SQL-функции (например, document_get_next_register_number будет источником document_number ). Документальный модуль Surypus теперь опирается на новую формализацию флагов и сохранённые SQL-функции. Следующий тикет — завершить UI/ETL/отчёты, оперируя этими invariants.

docs.text: Module 02 — HR / Payroll Следующий крупный модуль после документов — управление персоналом и расчёт заработной платы: правила валидности начислений и взаимосвязь с бухгалтерскими документами уже описаны в исходной реализации ( salary.cpp , Objstaff.cpp , v_staff.cpp ). 1. Анализ SalaryCore::Validate требует: числа идентификаторов положительные, Beg <= End , Amount в пределах серебряной десяти, Flags == 0 , ссылки на счета ( LinkBillID , GenBillID , RByGenBill ) в допустимом диапазоне. SalaryCore::Put блокирует пересечение периодов с теми же PostID + SalChargeID , чтобы не было двух записей за один период. Если найдена запись с точным совпадением периода, она обновляется, иначе вставляется новая. Calc() суммирует суммы по заданному PostID + SalChargeID и может возвращать как абсолютную сумму, так и среднее ( avg флаг). GetListByObject и др. — это фильтры для отчётов. 2. Что уже есть в Surypus Схема HR ( config/schema_hr.sql ) содержит таблицы отделов, должностей и сотрудников, а уже существующие функции ( hire_employee , calc_emp_salary ). Нет таблиц зарплатных начислений и прикладной логики, которая защищает от перекрытия периодов, разносит начисления по сотрудникам и связывает их с документами. 3. План переноса / уникализации SQL-схемы : добавить schema_hr_salary.sql с таблицами hr_salary , hr_salary_charge , hr_salary_link и индексы. Уникальность — (employee_id, charge_id, period_start, period_end) и CHECK (period_start <= period_end) . LiquidHaskell-модули : создать Core.HR.Types и Domain.HR с типами SalaryRecord , SalaryCharge , PayPeriod , EmployeeSalarySummary . Внедрить инварианты amount >= 0 , period_start <= period_end , charge_id > 0 , non-overlapping (для записей в одном вызове) и calcPeriodSum . Stored procedures : расширить sql/procedures.sql с create_salary_record , calc_salary_sum , hr_payroll_summary , resolve_salary_overlap (с RAISE EXCEPTION при дублировании). Добавить HASQL обёртки DB.Payroll . Hasql/Domain/API : добавить модуль DB.Payroll с listSalaryRecords , createSalaryRecord , getSalarySummary . Обновить APIServer (JWT-миддлваре) маршрут /api/v1/hr/salaries (GET, POST) и /api/v1/hr/payrolls/summary , а также hrRoutes для должностей/сотрудников с CRUD. QML/Reports/CI/test : добавить QML-формы для HR → Сотрудники → Начисления , Jasper-отчёт payroll_summary.jrxml , и property-based тесты Domain.HR (наличие неотрицательных сумм, корректный период). Добавить CI-шаг stack test --fast включающий HR-тесты. Документация : описать API, SQL хранимые процедуры, invariants LiquidHaskell; обновить README и docs/engineering . 4. Интеграция Поддерживать связи SalaryTbl::LinkBillID → bill.id через Hasql и LinkBill (экспорт DB.Bill / DB.Payroll ). Повторно использовать employee / department / position из schema_hr.sql и HR API (т.е. новые hrRoutes должны опираться на эти таблицы). Отчёты Salary должны быть переписаны в Jasper+Pentaho, а не использовать Crystal Reports. 5. Следующие действия (немедленные) Создать schema_hr_salary.sql + записать новые функции в sql/procedures.sql . Реализовать Core.HR.Types и Domain.HR с LiquidHaskell. Добавить DB.Payroll , APIServer.hrRoutes + JWT, и протестировать Domain.HR . Обновить документацию и запуск init_db.sh / init_schema для новых объектов. 6. Property-based проверки Чтобы убедиться, что базовые invariants с заработной платой сохраняются, в test/Domain/HRSpec добавлены QuickCheck-свойства: calcSalaryPerDay × количество дней ≈ сумма за период (с учётом округлений clampNonNeg ); calcSalaryPerDay никогда не даёт отрицательных значений; validateSalaryRecord работает при любых неотрицательных суммах и корректных периодах. Эти свойства покрывают те же правила, что и SalaryCore::Calc , но в терминах LiquidHaskell-типов, поэтому любые будущие изменения обязательно должны проходить через stack test --test-arguments "--match HR" и через property-based проверку (в CI).

docs.text: Job Server / ETL Surypus реализует надёжную очередь задач (JobServer), которая позволяет запускать ETL-работы, импорт/экспорт данных, генерацию отчётов и синхронизацию внешних систем (Меркурий, Честный Знак, WMS). Мы численно перенесли основные элементы: SQL-ядро : config/schema_job_server.sql описывает таблицы job , job_dependency , job_result и просмотры очереди. Дополнительно, DB.Connection.initSchema создаёт упрощённую версию job с кодом ( code ), приоритетом, JSON-данными ( job_data ) и временными метками ( scheduled_at , started_at , completed_at ). Индексы по status / priority обеспечивают быстрый выбор. Hasql & домен : Domain.Job описывает типы JobRequest , JobRecord , JobFilter , JobStatus и формальные инварианты (например, priority ∈ [1,10] , код/название/тип не пусты). DB.JobQueue связывает Hasql с таблицей, реализуя enqueueJob , fetchPendingJob , listJobs , getJob , setJobStatus и логирование ( service_events ). Также агрегируются зависимости из job_dependency , которые отражаются в JobRecord.jobDependencies , и добавлена функция addJobDependency . API : APIServer.jobRoutes предоставляет REST: - POST /api/v1/jobs — создать задачу (валидируется validateJobRequest ) - GET /api/v1/jobs — лента задач с фильтрацией по статусу и типу - GET /api/v1/jobs/:id — детализированная запись - PATCH /api/v1/jobs/:id/status — меняет статусы ( pending , running , completed , failed , cancelled ) QML UI : Surypus/qml/Main.qml содержит новый раздел «Jobs», который отображает очередь задач, их статусы и ошибки, а также позволяет вручную обновлять список. ETL-подсистема : JobServer регулярно запускает SQL-скрипты ( sql/procedures.sql ), выполняет Jasper/Pentaho/Helical отчёты и синхронизацию с PostgreSQL через триггеры ( schema_job_server.sql ). Интеграция с core -модулями делится через job_data и JSON-параметры, а DB.JobQueue позволяет продвинутому ETL-сценарию обрабатывать зависимости ( job_dependency ) и ошибки (через error_message ). REST и UI : появился endpoint /api/v1/jobs/:id/dependencies , а QML-приложение теперь умеет показывать зависимости и создавать их вручную, что упрощает планирование ETL-графов и отчётов (Jasper/Pentaho/Helical). Тесты и CI : test/Domain/JobSpec.hs проверяет validateJobRequest и jobStatusFromText . GitHub Actions запускает stack test , обеспечивая контроль логики очереди. В следующих итерациях планируется расширить JobServer: ETL-графы (наследование от job_dependency , расчёт wait_time ) Интеграция с Jasper/Pentaho через REST-генераторы ( reports/ ) Webhook и WebSocket нотификации о смене статуса задач Сервис-перехватчики для автоматического запуска DB.JobQueue.fetchPendingJob из внешних наблюдателей. Snapshot job и фоновый worker Новый тип задачи person_summary_snapshot агрегирует данные из таблицы person (через get_person_summary() ) и сохраняет их в person_summary_snapshot . Это позволяет Jasper/Pentaho/Helical строить исторические отчёты по контрагентам. Чтобы процесс регулярно выполнялся, добавлен standalone worker: Surypus.JobRunner.processPendingJobs вызывает DB.JobQueue.fetchPendingJob , помечает задачу JobRunning , запускает run_person_summary_snapshot и фиксирует статус ( completed / failed ). Логи попадают в service_events , чтобы мониторить ETL/репорты. app/JobWorker.hs и новый executable surypus-job-worker стартуют worker с интервалом SURYPUS_JOB_INTERVAL (по умолчанию 30 секунд). Скрипт scripts/run_job_worker.sh упрощает развёртывание в systemd/container. API POST /api/v1/persons/summary/snapshots триггерит snapshot on-demand, а GET /api/v1/persons/summary/snapshots возвращает последние 20 срезов ( person_summary_snapshot ), что пригодно для QML/отчётов и Jasper/Pentaho/Helical. Дальнейшие домены и ETL Пока JobServer покрывает базовую обработку документов, следующая волна портирования должна: HR & Payroll — перенести salary / payroll документы через core/api → Hasql → postgreSQL (первичный план в docs/engineering/hr-payroll-module.md ), написать ETL-джобы для начислений (в Jasper/Pentaho/Helical) и добавить property-based tests на расчёт НДФЛ/ФОТ. Production & Hardware — добавить tech / work-order потоки в job_dependency , обеспечить ETL job для MRP (с использованием get_mrp_requirements() в PostgreSQL) и перенести отчёты о производстве ( production_work_order , tech_story ). Reports & ETL pipeline — каждая задача report_render должна фиксировать report_template , filters , generated_at и результат (PDF/JRXML/CSV); JobServer должен запускать jasperreports , pentaho-kettle и helical CLI через job_payload["report_engine"] . Job-side invariants — расширить Domain.Job с LiquidHaskell-инвариантами: jrPriority ∈ [1,10] , jrCode / jrName / jrType не пусты, jrPayload валидный JSON. Эти инварианты затем проверяются до вставки job в очередь, включая job_dependency . Следующие публикации будут включать: * план перевода Crystal Reports → Jasper/Pentaho/Helical; * документацию по ETL job dependencies и DB.JobQueue API; * отчёт о тестах (unit, property-based, API, CI).

docs.text: Модуль «Персоны» (Person) 1. Цель и мотивация Модуль Surypus.Person должен эмулировать и расширять функциональность PPObjPerson из (файлы Src/PPLib/person.cpp , Src/PPLib/v_person.cpp , Src/PPLib/objreg.cpp ). PPObjPerson ведёт учёт контрагентов, привязаны к регистрам (ИНН/КПП/ОГРН), банковским реквизитам, контактам и разделам CRM/HR. Он заботится о: целостности ИНН и КПП; синонимичности записей с записями из разных объектов ( PPObjPersonRelType , JobQueue , PPObjRegister ); строгом учёте связей, адресов, контактов; начислении скидок и кредитных лимитов (используются в PPObjBill::SearchCustomer , PPObjPerson::GetClientActivityStatistics ). 2. Стек Surypus и текущие артефакты LiquidHaskell : Domain.Person уже несёт инварианты personCredit >= 0 и 0 <= personDiscount <= 100 . Это ядро можно расширить, добавив validateINN / validateKPP с доказательствами. PostgreSQL : config/database_schema.sql создаёт persons.person и наследуемые таблицы employee/manager . Дополнительные скрипты ( config/schema_person.sql , config/schema_person_kind.sql и др.) расширяют адреса, контакты. Hasql : DB.Person и Domain.Person служат API-слоем, но пока обрывываются между схемой и API (например, в схеме person нет колонок address , credit_limit , discount , которые используются в запросах). REST : APIServer.personsRoutes уже реализует CRUD и фильтры по name/inn/kind/status . QML/Reports/Job : пока нет экранов/отчётов, но мы планируем QML-модуль «Контрагенты», ETL-инструменты и регулярные подкачки ( JobQueue ) для синхронизации с CRM-сервисами. 3. Необходимые инварианты и проверки INN и KPP — только цифры, длина 10 или 12 (см. PPObjPerson::CheckINN() , PPObjPerson::CheckKPP() в person.cpp ). Кредитный лимит и скидка — неотрицательные ( PPObjPerson::SetCreditLimit ), скидка не может превышать 100%. Каждая персона должна иметь хотя бы трёхзначный код/символьный идентификатор в person.code . Связи PersonRel не должны создавать циклов (аналог PPObjPersonRelType::CheckCycle ). Локализация адресов должна совпадать с репозиториями PersonLocation и PersonContact . Инварианты накладываются в LiquidHaskell на Person ( Domain.Person ) и PersonRel друг с другом. Пространство типов должно отражать эти ограничения и фиксировать их на этапе компиляции. 4. План реализации Схема PostgreSQL : удостовериться, что persons.person имеет столбцы code , address , phone , email , credit_limit , discount . Добавить ALTER TABLE в config/schema_person.sql или config/database_schema.sql , чтобы гарантировать их наличие независимо от порядка исполнения. Hasql/DB : согласовать декодеры с точным списком полей; добавить INSERT / UPDATE с контролем code и search_path . Core/Domain : расширить LiquidHaskell-инварианты ( validateINN , validateKPP ), описать PersonRel и PersonLocation как типы с доказательствами (например, PersonLocation не может быть одновременно isPrimary и isDefault для двух записей). API : усилить middleware с JWT/логгированием и расширить CRUD на PersonContact , PersonBankAccount , PersonLocation . UI/Reports/Jobs : представить qml/persons/ с формами, отчёты Jasper / Pentaho и расширенный JobQueue для синхронизации контрагентов. Тесты : свойство prop_person_credit_nonneg , таблицы с QuickCheck PersonRel (без циклов), интеграционный тест APIServer.personsRoutes . 5. Текущие действия Выделить модуль Person как первый в контуре реинжиниринга; Привести наименования schema (уникальные schema_Core_Document_Register , schema_PPObjRegister_Register ) и задокументировать их; Проверить alignment схемы persons.person с DB.Person , включая code / credit_limit . Создать агрегированные отчёты/хранимые процедуры (например, get_person_summary() ), чтобы job-сервер мог эвакуировать KPI по контрагентам и передавать их в Jasper/Pentaho/Helical. Сделать snapshot job ( run_person_summary_snapshot ), который периодически срабатывает в job-очереди и переносит KPI в person_summary_snapshot , позволяя QML/UI строить графики трендов и наполнять отчёты Jasper/Pentaho/Helical. 6. Источники Src/PPLib/person.cpp , Src/PPLib/v_person.cpp , Src/PPLib/objreg.cpp . Surypus: Domain.Person , DB.Person , APIServer.personsRoutes , config-схемы.

docs.text: Module 03 — Production / Hardware После стабилизации Document и HR/Payroll следующий критический блок — производство и связанный Hardware (MRP, техкарты, нормативы, job-сервер). Общий сценарий описан в tech.cpp , ppbuild.cpp , ppordr.cpp и смежных файлах: технологическая карта ( PPObjTech ), ресурсоёмкие заказы ( PPObjWorkOrder ), перемещения между складами и связка с BillCore / AccTurn . 1. Что делает исходная реализация (фокус на tech.cpp ) PPObjTech хранит технологические структуры ( TechTbl ), которые связывают процессор (документ Processor ) с товарами, формулами и типами операций ( TECK_AUTO , TECK_MANUAL ). TechLines ( TGSArray ) управляют списком GoodsID с коэффициентами ( Sign ) и формулами; реализованы методы GetGoodsList , AddItem , SearchGoods_ , CreateAutoTech . Это позволяет из MRP автоматически подставлять компоненты и найти техкарту по сырью. PPObjTech::GenerateCode увеличивает глобальный счетчик TecCounter в PPObjProcessor и генерирует уникальные коды (с префиксом TLNG для tooling). Surypus должен сохранить этот счётчик в одной из таблиц (например, tech_counter ) и гарантировать атомарность через транзакции. PPObjTech::SearchAuto и SearchAutoForGoodsCreation ищут автоматические техкарты по принадлежности товара к группе ( GoodsObj::BelongToGroup ). Производственные документы полагаются на эти поиски для определения компонентов, и они должны быть пока Hasql строит профили. 2. Где Surypus должен усиливать архитектуру SQL-схемы : создать schema_tech.sql , schema_work_order.sql , schema_mrp.sql . Таблицы: - tech_card (id, processor_id, goods_group_id, kind, formula, flags, code); - tech_line (tech_id, line_no, goods_id, qty, sign, formula_text); - work_order (id, code, goods_id, qty_plan, qty_released, status, scheduled_at, start_at, end_at, processor_id); - work_order_line и work_order_movement (статики для склада, запасов). Добавить индексы на processor_id , code , status , goods_id . Уникальность: (processor_id, goods_id, kind, code) и (work_order.code) . Constraints: - qty_plan >= 0 , qty_released >= 0 , status ∈ {0..4} (например, pending/running/completed/cancelled/failed); - tech_line.qty >= 0 , sign ∈ {-1,0,1} . LiquidHaskell-инварианты : - Тип TechLine (часть Core.Production.Types ) с qty >= 0 , sign из дискретного множества, formula не пустой для автоматических линий. - WorkOrder с qtyPlanned >= qtyReleased , status корректен (в перечислении WorkOrderStatus ), schedule & dates согласованы ( scheduled_at <= start <= end ), processor / goods обязательно существует в домене. - MRPRequirement (тип Sec). calcMRPNeed должен доказывать, что суммарный спрос равен сумме потребного ранее минус уже выделенные запасы (инвариант Σ need >= 0 ). Hasql и Stored procedures : - Внести функции create_tech_card , create_tech_line , find_auto_tech(cards) , reserve_mrp_requirements , release_work_order , complete_work_order . Они должны включать RAISE EXCEPTION при нарушениях (наличие дублей, нехватка ресурсов, неоднозначный статус). - Добавить процедуры, моделирующие BillCore::Post для WorkOrder (создание acc_turn / stock_movement , обновление lot ). Вызов calc_stock_balance / fifo_select_lots уже есть — надо адаптировать. API/QML/JobServer : - Расширить DB.Production / Domain.Production на новые endpoints: GET /production/work-orders , POST /production/work-orders , POST /production/work-orders/:id/release , POST /production/work-orders/:id/complete , GET /production/tech . - Добавить JWT-мидлвар, логирование, property tests (например, проверка, что суммарный qty_released <= qty_plan ). - JobServer: job -типы production_release , production_snapshot . DB.JobQueue.enqueueJob должен запускать MRP-джобы (генерация Jasper/Pentaho/Helical production_mrp.jrxml ). - QML: создать раздел “Production” с формами TechCard , WorkOrder , визуализация MRP graph . Reports : - Jasper/Pentaho: production_mrp.jrxml , work_order_status.jrxml , tech_card_bom.jrxml . - JobServer => report_render job production_work_order , production_capacity . - Интеграция Reports (REST: /reports , /reports/:name ), Reports.ReportDef → SQL/HR result via calc_stock_balance / get_lot_bounds . 3. Связь с Hardware Hardware (например, PPObjProcessor , PPObjProcessorConfig ) задаёт ресурсы, которые включают машины и инструменты ( processor + tech ). Нужно связать tech_card.processor_id с Hardware (эмулировать PPProcessor и PPProcessorConfig ), включая атомарную генерацию кода ( TecCounter → tech_counter ), чтобы Surypus мог формировать заявки на машины. Добавить таблицу hardware_resource , hardware_schedule (для планирования), инварианты: ресурс не используется одновременно двумя заказами, scheduled_at + occupied_until согласованы. 4. Проверки и CI QuickCheck: prop_release_not_exceed_plan , prop_tech_qty_nonneg , prop_mrp_conservation . Интеграции: stack test --test-arguments "--match Production" и --match HR (после стабилизации vector / directory ). CI ( .github/workflows/ci.yml ) обязуется: сборка, тесты, отчёты, stack exec scripts/check_schema_uniqueness.sh , stack exec hindent , stack exec hlint . 5. Следующие задачи Описать таблицы/schemas (см. config/schema_production.sql , config/schema_tech.sql ), добавить миграции init_db.sh . Реализовать Core.Production.Types / Domain.Production с LiquidHaskell-типами, DB.Production (Hasql) и API/QML/JobServer. Написать отчёты Jasper/Pentaho/Helical, job-джобы, property tests. После каждого блока добавлять документацию в docs/engineering и фиксировать прогон stack test (и eventual stack test --match Production ).

docs.text: Отчёты: Jasper / Pentaho / Helical встроенный генератор отчётов report_engine (например PPReport , CrystalReport ). Surypus перепроектирует отчётную подсистему в несколько компонентов: Математические шаблоны — каждую Crystal-форму ( report/*.rpt ) мы описали как ReportDef (см. Surypus/src/Surypus/Reports.hs и Surypus/src/Reports.hs ). Сегодня доступны шаблоны: * sales_daily.jrxml — ежедневные продажи (Jasper) * inventory.jrxml — остатки по складам (Pentaho) * balance_sheet.jrxml — финансы (Helical) SQL-поддержка — sql/procedures.sql содержит calc_bill_totals , calc_stock_balance , calc_vat , и другие подпрограммы, ранее реализованные на C++ в objbill.cpp , objstor.cpp . Эти процедуры являются входом для Jasper/Pentaho и могут вызываться напрямую из JobServer. REST-доступ — APIServer.reportRoutes отдаёт метаданные отчётов ( /reports , /reports/:name ), а QML UI ( reportPage ) позволяет пользователю просматривать описания и SQL-фрагменты до запуска. Интеграция Jasper/Pentaho/Helical : * Jasper ( *.jrxml ) содержит параметры (даты, фильтры, контрагенты) и может генерировать PDF/HTML через jasperreports CLI. * Pentaho использовать Pentaho Data Integration для ETL-потоков, преобразовывающих данные из PostgreSQL в CSV/OLAP. * Helical задействует регенерацию OLAP-кубов на основе job / report данных, сохраняя исторические снимки. JobServer ↔ Reports — каждая задача может ссылаться на report_template_id в job_data , что позволяет автоматизировать генерацию отчётов по расписанию (см. Domain.Job и DB.JobQueue.enqueueJob ). Мониторинг — отчёты регистрируются в service_events , job -статусах и выводятся на QML-дэшборде (ниже) через reportModel . Scheduled Rendering — новая таблица report_schedule и endpoints /reports/schedules позволяют создать cron-расписание для любого ReportDef . Каждый запуск создаёт задачу report_render с payload { scheduleId } , которую обрабатывает worker surypus-job-worker . Результат сохраняется в report_render_snapshot и доступен по GET /reports/schedules/:id/snapshots , поэтому Jasper/Pentaho/Helical могут подхватывать исторические JRXML. Следующие улучшения: Поддержка Pentaho / Helical через REST -обёртки (см. Surypus/web/ ). Автоматическая публикация PDF на reports.surypus.local . Версионирование шаблонов в reports/ (Git + Jenkins).

docs.text: Унификация схем PostgreSQL Контекст При портировании в Surypus мы сохраняем множество SQL-скриптов, отражающих разные домены: accounting, finance, documents, legal, common и т.д. Некоторые объекты в старых скриптах переотражаются (например, AccSheet используется и в Core.Accounting , и в Core.Finance , а Register / RegisterType — и в PPObjRegister , и в Core.Document ). Без разграничения название schema_acc_sheet.sql могло содержать несколько схем, что затрудняло валидацию. Что сделано schema_Core_Accounting_AccSheet.sql и schema_Core_Finance_AccSheet.sql теперь содержат разные таблицы ( acc_sheet_accounting vs acc_sheet_finance ), что позволяет освободить пространство имён и не пересекаться по индексам или триггерам. В schema_Core_Document_Register.sql и schema_PPObjRegister_Register.sql одинаковая view v_active_registers конфликтовала, когда оба скрипта выполнялись последовательно. Мы переименовали их в v_core_document_active_registers и v_ppobj_active_registers , чтобы: - избежать перезаписи одной и той же view при инициализации; - дать возможность обращаться к каждой view отдельно (в отчётах или job-сервере); - позволить под конкретный трудовой регистр (Core.Document vs PPObjRegister) добавлять свои индикаторы деятельности. В docs/engineering/person-module.md отражён план дальнейшей выверки схем, включая приведение новых таблиц к принципам уникальности (отдельные таблицы/представления для регистраций, контактных сведений и т.д.). Следующие шаги Проверить остальные schema_* на пересечения имён объектов ( CREATE VIEW , CREATE FUNCTION , INSERT INTO с фиксированными id ) и задокументировать границы доменов. Добавить миграцию, которая явно именует таблицы/представления при пересечении (например, document_register_type vs legal_register_type ) и контролирует порядок выполнения скриптов. scripts/check_schema_uniqueness.sh готов, его следует запускать перед stack test и включить в CI, чтобы автоматически выявлять перекрытия объектов.

docs.text: Testing Guide How to write and run tests in Surypus. Running Tests All Tests stack test Single Test Group # Run tests matching a pattern stack test --match "VAT" # Run specific spec stack test --test-arguments "-m \"НДС 20%\"" Single Test File stack test --test-arguments "test/Test.hs" Verbose Output stack test --verbose QuickCheck Properties stack test --test-arguments "--quickcheck" Test Structure Surypus/test/ ├── Test.hs -- Main test suite ├── Finance/ │ ├── TaxSpec.hs -- Tax calculation tests │ ├── AccountingSpec.hs │ └── BillSpec.hs ├── Surypus/ │ └── ValidationSpec.hs -- Validation logic tests ├── Integration/ │ ├── APISpec.hs -- API endpoint tests │ ├── DatabaseSpec.hs -- DB tests │ └── PerformanceSpec.hs └── Fixtures/ └── TestFixtures.hs -- Shared test data Writing Tests Unit Tests (Hspec) module Domain.TaxSpec where import Test.Hspec import Core.Tax spec_vat_calculation :: Spec spec_vat_calculation = describe "calcVAT" $ do it "calculates 20% VAT on 1000" $ calcVAT 1000 ( Decimal 20 ) ` shouldBe ` Decimal 200 it "returns 0 for negative amount" $ calcVAT ( Decimal ( - 100 )) ( Decimal 20 ) ` shouldBe ` Decimal 0 Property-Based Tests (QuickCheck) import Test.QuickCheck prop_vat_nonnegative :: Property prop_vat_nonnegative = forAll genAmountAndRate $ \ ( amount , rate ) -> calcVAT amount rate >= 0 -- Generate valid inputs genAmountAndRate :: Gen ( Decimal , Decimal ) genAmountAndRate = do amount <- Decimal . abs <$> choose ( 100 , 100000000 :: Int64 ) rate <- Decimal . abs <$> choose ( 0 , 100 :: Int64 ) pure ( amount , rate ) Integration Tests module Integration.APISpec where import Test.Hspec import Network.Wai ( Application ) import Network.Wai.Test ( sresponseStatus , SResponse ) spec_api_endpoints :: Spec spec_api_endpoints = describe "API Endpoints" $ do it "GET /health returns 200" $ do response <- simpleHttp "http://localhost:8080/health" responseStatus response ` shouldBe ` Status 200 "OK" TestFixtures Shared test data for consistent testing: module Fixtures.TestFixtures where import Surypus.Types -- Sample company testCompany :: Company testCompany = Company { cId = 1 , cName = "Test Company" , cInn = "1234567890" } -- Sample tax rate testTaxRate20 :: TaxRate testTaxRate20 = TaxRate { trId = 1 , trName = "НДС 20%" , trRate = Decimal 20 , trFlags = 0 } -- Sample goods testGoods :: Goods testGoods = Goods { gId = 1 , gName = "Test Product" , gCode = "TEST001" } CI Pipeline GitHub Actions Workflow name : Test on : [ push , pull_request ] jobs : test : runs-on : ubuntu-latest steps : - uses : actions/checkout@v4 - uses : haskell/actions/setup@v2 with : ghc-version : '9.12.4' - run : stack build - run : stack test - run : hlint src/ Running Locally # Full pipeline stack build && stack test && hlint src/ Test Coverage # Generate coverage report (if HPC enabled) stack test --coverage Best Practices Use descriptive test names - "calculates 20% VAT on 1000" not "test 1" Test edge cases - Zero, negative, boundary values Use property-based testing - For mathematical operations Keep fixtures modular - Separate by domain Test error paths - Not just happy path Name QuickCheck generators - genAmountAndRate not gen'

docs.text: Surypus Event Sourcing Examples Quick Start 1. Receive Stock -- Create tenant and user first INSERT INTO tenants ( tenant_name , tenant_code ) VALUES ( 'Test Tenant' , 'test001' ); -- Receive stock (creates LotCreated and StockReceived events) SELECT cmd_inventory_receive_stock ( gen_random_uuid (), -- aggregate_id ( SELECT tenant_id FROM tenants LIMIT 1 ), NULL , -- user_id gen_random_uuid (), -- goods_id gen_random_uuid (), -- location_id 100 . 0 , -- qty 10 . 0 , -- cost 15 . 0 , -- price 'LOT-001' , -- lot_number NULL , -- expiry_date NULL -- document_ref ); 2. Issue Stock (FIFO) -- Issue stock (creates LotConsumed and StockIssued events) SELECT * FROM cmd_inventory_issue_stock ( aggregate_id , -- same aggregate tenant_id , NULL , -- user_id goods_id , -- same goods location_id , -- same location 50 . 0 , -- qty_needed NULL , -- document_ref NULL -- expected_version ); -- Returns: lot_id, qty_used, cost, amount for each lot consumed 3. Check Stock Balance -- Query projection (read model) SELECT * FROM stock_get_balance ( goods_id , location_id ); -- Or query specific goods across all locations SELECT * FROM projection_stock_balance WHERE goods_id = '...' ; 4. Create and Post Bill -- Create bill SELECT cmd_bill_create ( gen_random_uuid (), tenant_id , NULL , 'INV-001' , CURRENT_DATE , person_id , location_id , op_kind_id , 'Notes here' , NULL ); -- Add line SELECT cmd_bill_add_line ( bill_aggregate_id , tenant_id , NULL , NULL , -- line_id (auto-generated) goods_id , 10 . 0 , -- quantity 100 . 0 , -- price 0 . 0 , -- discount 20 . 0 , -- vat_rate NULL -- expected_version ); -- Post bill (triggers stock movements and accounting entries) SELECT cmd_bill_post ( bill_aggregate_id , tenant_id , NULL , NULL -- expected_version ); 5. Saga Execution -- Start sales order saga SELECT saga_create ( 'sales_order' , gen_random_uuid (), tenant_id , input_data : = '{ "inventory_aggregate": "...", "bill_aggregate": "...", "goods_id": "...", "location_id": "...", "person_id": "...", "qty": 10.0, "price": 100.0, "cost": 50.0, "vat_rate": 20.0, "bill_code": "INV-001" }' :: jsonb ); -- Execute steps one by one SELECT saga_execute_step ( saga_id , tenant_id , NULL ); -- Check status SELECT * FROM saga_get_status ( saga_id ); Haskell Examples Event Store Operations {-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-} import Surypus.Core.EventStore main :: IO () main = do -- Create event store connection let store = mkEventStore "postgresql://..." -- Append event result <- appendEvent store aggregateId "Inventory" "StockReceived" ( object [ "qty" .= ( 100 :: Double ), "cost" .= ( 10 :: Double )]) tenantId Nothing -- expected version case result of Left err -> putStrLn $ "Error: " ++ err Right ( eventId , seqNum ) -> do putStrLn $ "Event appended: " ++ show eventId putStrLn $ "Sequence: " ++ show seqNum -- Get events events <- getEvents store aggregateId mapM_ print events Inventory Operations import Surypus.Domain.Inventory main :: IO () main = do -- Create initial state let stock = emptyStock -- Define commands let receiveCmd = ReceiveStock { rcGoodsId = goodsId , rcLocationId = locationId , rcQty = 100.0 , rcCost = 10.0 } -- Execute command case executeCommand stock receiveCmd of Left violation -> print violation Right ( newStock , events ) -> do putStrLn $ "New stock qty: " ++ show ( unQuantity $ currentQty newStock ) putStrLn $ "Events generated: " ++ show ( length events ) Saga Orchestration import Surypus.Core.Saga main :: IO () main = do -- Define saga let salesOrderSaga = Saga { sagaType = "sales_order" , sagaSteps = [ Step "reserve_stock" reserveStockHandler , Step "create_bill" createBillHandler , Step "post_bill" postBillHandler , Step "issue_stock" issueStockHandler ] } -- Execute saga result <- runSaga salesOrderSaga sagaInput case result of SagaCompleted -> putStrLn "Saga completed successfully" SagaFailed err -> putStrLn $ "Saga failed: " ++ err SagaCompensated -> putStrLn "Saga compensated after failure" REST API Examples cURL Examples # Receive stock curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/inventory/receive \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-API-Key: your-key" \ -d '{ "aggregateId": "...", "goodsId": "...", "locationId": "...", "qty": 100, "cost": {"currency": "USD", "amountCents": 10000} }' # Issue stock curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/inventory/issue \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "aggregateId": "...", "goodsId": "...", "locationId": "...", "qty": 50, "method": "FIFO" }' # Get stock balance curl "http://localhost:3000/api/v1/inventory/balance?goodsId=...&locationId=..." # Start saga curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/sagas \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "sagaType": "sales_order", "correlationId": "...", "inputData": {...} }' Event Streaming Subscribe to Events import Surypus.Client.EventStream main :: IO () main = do -- Connect to event stream withEventStream "localhost:9092" $ \ stream -> do -- Subscribe to inventory events subscribe stream [ "surypus.events.inventory.*" ] -- Process events forever $ do event <- nextEvent stream case eventType event of "StockReceived" -> handleStockReceived event "StockIssued" -> handleStockIssued event _ -> return () Monitoring Queries -- System health SELECT * FROM metrics_get_system_health (); -- Event processing stats SELECT * FROM metrics_event_stats_hourly WHERE hour >= NOW () - INTERVAL '1 hour' ; -- Projection lag SELECT * FROM metrics_projection_lag_current ; -- Saga execution stats SELECT * FROM metrics_saga_stats_daily WHERE day >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 days' ; -- Command execution stats SELECT * FROM metrics_command_stats_daily ; Common Patterns 1. Replay Projections -- Truncate and rebuild projection TRUNCATE projection_fifo_lots ; TRUNCATE projection_stock_balance ; -- Replay events (would be done by projection service) SELECT rebuild_all_projections (); 2. Temporal Query -- State at specific point in time SELECT aggregate_id , event_type , event_data FROM event_store WHERE aggregate_id = '...' AND created_at <= '2024-01-01 00:00:00' ORDER BY sequence_number ; 3. Event Audit Trail -- Full history for aggregate SELECT es . created_at , es . event_type , es . event_data , es . user_id , es . correlation_id FROM event_store es WHERE es . aggregate_id = '...' ORDER BY es . sequence_number ; Testing Examples Unit Test with InMemory Store import Test.Hspec import Surypus.Test.InMemory spec :: Spec spec = do describe "Inventory Aggregate" $ do it "should maintain quantity invariant" $ do let stock = emptyStock receive = ReceiveStock { ... } case executeCommand stock receive of Right ( newStock , _ ) -> do unQuantity ( currentQty newStock ) ` shouldBe ` 100.0 Left err -> expectationFailure $ show err Property Test import Test.QuickCheck prop_quantityConserved :: Stock -> Command -> Property prop_quantityConserved stock cmd = case executeCommand stock cmd of Left _ -> property True Right ( newStock , _ ) -> let oldTotal = sumLots ( stockLots stock ) newTotal = sumLots ( stockLots newStock ) in case cmd of ReceiveStock { .. } -> newTotal == oldTotal + rcQty IssueStock { .. } -> oldTotal == newTotal + isQty _ -> True

docs.text: GraphQL Client Migration Plan Issue: US-3-7 — Move external consumers from REST endpoints to the GraphQL proxy at /graphql . 1. Current Architecture REST Endpoints (to be deprecated) GET /api/v1/bills → listBills GET /api/v1/goods → listGoods GET /api/v1/persons → listPersons POST /api/v1/payments → listPayments GET /api/v1/orders → listOrders GET /api/v1/dashboard/summary ... GraphQL Proxy All REST endpoints are mapped one-to-one to the GraphQL layer at POST /graphql : { "query" : "<operation_name>" , "variables" : { ... } } Operation (query) REST endpoint Response type bills GET /api/v1/bills Bills[] goods GET /api/v1/goods Goods[] persons GET /api/v1/persons Persons[] payments POST /api/v1/payments Payments[] orders GET /api/v1/orders Orders[] dashboardKPI GET /api/v1/dashboard/summary DashboardStats deals GET /api/v1/crm/deals Deals[] contacts GET /api/v1/crm/contacts Contacts[] companies GET /api/v1/crm/companies Companies[] pipelineForecast GET /api/v1/crm/pipeline Pipeline[] pipelineStages GET /api/v1/crm/stages Stages[] 2. Migration Steps for Consumers 2.1 Bulk / Script Migration (Python example) import requests API_URL = "https://api.example.com/graphql" HEADERS = { "Content-Type" : "application/json" , "Authorization" : "Bearer ..." } def execute ( query : str , variables : dict = None ) -> dict : payload = { "query" : query } if variables : payload [ "variables" ] = variables resp = requests . post ( API_URL , json = payload , headers = HEADERS ) resp . raise_for_status () return resp . json () # Old: GET /api/v1/bills?limit=100&offset=0 # New: result = execute ( "bills" , { "limit" : 100 , "offset" : 0 }) bills = result [ "data" ] errors = result . get ( "errors" , []) Variables accepted by most operations: Variable Type Description limit Int Page size (default: 100) offset Int Offset for skip filter JSON object Field-value pairs for filtering sort JSON array ["field:asc", "field2:desc"] status String E.g. "active" , "cancelled" 2.2 Frontend Migration (React example) const client = new ApolloClient ({ uri : "/graphql" , headers : { Authorization : `Bearer ${ token } ` } }); // Old: // const bills = await api.get('/bills?limit=100'); // New: const { data , loading , error } = useQuery ( gql `{ bills(limit: 100) { id number status total } }` , { errorPolicy : "all" } ); 3. Deprecation Timeline Phase Date Action 1 2026-10-16 GraphQL proxy enabled (already live) 2 2026-11-01 Deprecation warning added to REST response headers 3 2027-01-01 REST endpoints return HTTP 410 (Gone) 4. Monitoring & Rollout Enable @surypus/api-monitoring to track: /graphql request volume GraphQL error rates Client-by-client adoption (parsed from user-agent) Set up alert if REST error rate exceeds 0 after Phase 2. 5. Known Limitations All operations return flat objects; nested filtering not yet supported. Pagination: cursor-based ( after / before ) coming in Phase 4. File uploads: must use presigned S3 URLs; GraphQL attachment support pending.

docs.text: How Accounting Works Overview Surypus implements double-entry bookkeeping following the accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Equity Every financial transaction must preserve this balance. Core Concepts Debit — left-side entry that increases assets or expenses, decreases liabilities/equity/revenue Credit — right-side entry that increases liabilities/equity/revenue, decreases assets/expenses Journal Entry — a record of one or more debit/credit pairs Ledger — the collection of all accounts and their balances Module Structure Core.Accounting ├── Types -- Accounting types (JournalEntry, LedgerAccount) ├── Journal -- Journal entry operations ├── Ledger -- Ledger balance computation └── Validation -- Accounting invariant checks Journal Entry Lifecycle Create — a new JournalEntry is created with debit/credit lines Validate — validateJournalEntry checks that total debits = total credits Post — posted entries update the ledger balances Close — period-end closing entries transfer temporary account balances Invariants -- | Total debits must equal total credits for every journal entry. -- -- >>> validateJournalEntry (JournalEntry [Debit 100, Credit 100]) -- True validateJournalEntry :: JournalEntry -> Bool Related Modules Core.Tax — tax calculations on accounting entries Core.Inventory — inventory valuation methods Finance.Accounting — financial reporting See Also Architecture: Event Sourcing Database: Accounting schema API: Accounting endpoints

docs.text: How Event Store Works Overview Surypus uses an Event Store pattern for auditability and event sourcing capabilities. Core Concepts Event — an immutable fact that happened in the system Event Stream — a sequence of events for an aggregate Snapshot — a periodic checkpoint of aggregate state Event Bus — publishes events to subscribers Event Store Module Structure Surypus.EventStore ├── Types -- Event types (Event, EventStream, Snapshot) ├── Append -- Event append operations ├── Query -- Event query and reading ├── Snapshot -- Snapshot management └── PubSub -- Event publishing and subscriptions Event Lifecycle Domain Event │ ▼ Append ──► Event Store (immutable log) │ ▼ Publish ──► Event Bus ──► Subscribers │ ▼ Snapshot (periodic) ──► Aggregate state cache Event Types Event Description BillCreated A new bill was created BillApproved A bill was approved PaymentReceived Payment was recorded InventoryAdjusted Inventory was adjusted UserRoleChanged RBAC role was modified Snapshots Snapshots are taken after N events to avoid replaying the entire stream: -- | Create or retrieve a snapshot for an aggregate. -- -- >>> getSnapshot "bill-123" -- Just (Snapshot "bill-123" 42 events) getSnapshot :: AggregateId -> IO ( Maybe Snapshot ) Related Modules EventBus — event publishing Core.Accounting — accounting events Core.Inventory — inventory events See Also Architecture: Event Sourcing Persistence Guide

docs.text: How Inventory Lifecycle Works Overview Surypus tracks inventory through a complete lifecycle from procurement to consumption/sale. Core Concepts Goods — product catalog items Stock — physical inventory holdings at warehouses Lot — a batch of goods with specific properties (expiry, manufacture date) Movement — any change in stock quantity (receipt, issue, transfer) Lifecycle Stages Procurement Receipt Storage Sale/Consumption │ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ Purchase Goods Received Stock on Hand Goods Shipped Order → Lot Created → Lot Picked → Stock Reduced Key Operations Receive Goods — receiveGoods creates a new Goods record and initial Stock Issue Stock — issueStock reduces stock, creates a Lot if needed Transfer — transferStock moves stock between warehouses Adjust — adjustStock corrects inventory counts (shrinkage, damage) Invariants -- | Stock rest must equal initial + receipts - issues. -- -- >>> checkStockRest initial receipts issues -- True checkStockRest :: Int -> Int -> Int -> Bool Valuation Methods Surypus supports multiple inventory valuation methods: FIFO — First In, First Out LIFO — Last In, First Out Weighted Average — Average cost per unit Related Modules Core.Inventory — inventory types and operations Core.Stock — stock management Core.Goods — goods catalog Core.Warehouse — warehouse management See Also Architecture: Domain Model Database: Inventory schema

docs.text: How JWT Authentication Works Overview Surypus uses JSON Web Tokens (JWT) for stateless authentication and authorization. Core Concepts Access Token — short-lived token for API requests Refresh Token — long-lived token for obtaining new access tokens Claims — payload data embedded in the JWT (user ID, roles, permissions) Secret — symmetric key used to sign tokens Module Structure Surypus.JWT ├── Types -- JWT types (Token, Claims, JwtHeader) ├── Generate -- Token generation and signing ├── Validate -- Token validation and claims verification └── Refresh -- Token refresh logic Token Flow Client API Server Auth Service │ │ │ │── login (credentials) ────▶│ │ │ │── verify credentials ──▶│ │ │◀── access + refresh ────│ │◀── access token + refresh ─│ │ │ │ │ │── access token ───────────▶│ │ │ │── validate JWT ─────────▶│ │ │◀── claims + permissions ─│ │ │ │ │◀── response ──────────────│ │ Claims Structure -- | JWT claims for Surypus authentication. -- -- >>> jwtClaims (User "alice" [Role "Admin"]) "exp" -- Claims {sub = "alice", roles = [Role "Admin"], ...} data Claims = Claims { sub :: UserId , roles :: [ Role ] , permissions :: [ Permission ] , exp :: Int } Security Properties Tokens are signed with HS256 (HMAC-SHA256) Access tokens expire after 15 minutes Refresh tokens expire after 7 days Token revocation is checked against the revocation list Related Modules Surypus.RBAC — RBAC and permissions Surypus.Types — core types See Also RBAC Guide API: Auth endpoints

docs.text: How Persistence Works Overview Surypus uses PostgreSQL as its primary persistence layer, with stored procedures for heavy computations. Core Concepts Migrations — versioned SQL files in sql/migrations/ (V000–V1005) Stored Procedures — business logic executed in PostgreSQL Persistent — type-safe ORM layer for Haskell Esqueleto — type-safe SQL builder Architecture Haskell Application │ ├── persistent ──────► PostgreSQL tables ├── esqueleto ──────► Type-safe SQL queries ├── raw SQL ────────► Stored procedures └── migration ───────► Schema versioning Migration System All database changes go through sql/migrations/ : File Description V001__initial_schema.sql Companies, persons, goods V002__goods.sql Inventory tables V003__bills.sql Bills and orders V004__accounting.sql Accounting tables V005__payroll.sql Payroll tables V006__jobs.sql Job scheduling V007__auth.sql Authentication V008__audit.sql Audit logging V009__rbac_store.sql RBAC tables V1005__payroll_results.sql Payroll results Running Migrations # Apply all pending migrations psql -h localhost -U surypus -d surypus -f sql/migrations/init_db.sh # Apply single migration psql -h localhost -U surypus -d surypus -f sql/migrations/V009__rbac_store.sql Stored Procedures Heavy computations live in PostgreSQL: calc_vat() — VAT calculation calc_bill_totals() — Bill total computation get_lot_bounds() — Lot boundary queries Related Modules Surypus.DAL — Database access layer Surypus.Queries — Query builders Surypus.Mutations — Mutation operations See Also Database Documentation Architecture

docs.text: How RBAC Works Overview Surypus implements Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) for multi-tenant operations. Core Concepts Tenant — an isolated organizational unit (company, department) Role — a named set of permissions (e.g., Admin , Accountant , Manager ) Permission — a fine-grained action right (e.g., bill:create , report:view ) User — an authenticated person assigned one or more roles Policy — a rule that evaluates whether a user-action-resource tuple is allowed RBAC Module Structure Surypus.RBAC ├── Types -- RBAC types (Role, Permission, Policy) ├── Store -- Persistent RBAC storage operations ├── Evaluator -- Policy evaluation engine └── SelfHeal -- Automatic RBAC consistency repair Permission Model Permissions follow the pattern resource:action : Permission Description bill:create Create new bills bill:approve Approve bills report:view View financial reports admin:users Manage users and roles inventory:adjust Adjust inventory counts Policy Evaluation -- | Check whether a user is authorized for an action on a resource. -- -- >>> canUser (User "alice" [Role "Accountant"]) "bill:create" "bill:123" -- True canUser :: User -> Permission -> ResourceId -> Bool Tenant Isolation Each tenant has its own namespace: Tenant: acme-corp ├── Roles: Admin, Accountant, Manager ├── Users: alice (Accountant), bob (Admin) └── Resources: bills.*, reports.* Self-Healing The RBAC self-heal module ( rbac_self_heal_incremental.sql ) automatically: Detects orphaned roles (no users assigned) Detects missing permissions on existing roles Detects inconsistent policy assignments Generates repair SQL statements Related Modules Surypus.RBAC.Store — persistent storage Surypus.RBAC.Types — type definitions Surypus.JWT — authentication integration See Also Architecture: Security Database: RBAC schema

docs.text: Blocking Issues Policy This document describes how Surypus handles blocking issues and what contributors can do when their work is blocked. ---Inspired by maintainer communities worldwide. Thank you to everyone who shared their experiences. What Are Blocking Issues? Blocking issues are issues that prevent contributors from making progress on their work. They can take many forms: Unanswered questions - The contributor needs information to proceed Unclear priorities - The contributor doesn't know if their work aligns with project goals Missing reviews - The contributor's PR hasn't been reviewed in a timely manner Conflicting feedback - Different maintainers have given conflicting guidance Technical blockers - Dependencies, infrastructure, or other technical issues If you're experiencing any of these, this policy is for you. Identifying a Blocking Issue You may have a blocking issue if: You've been waiting for a response for more than the stated response time You're unsure about the direction of your contribution You've received conflicting feedback and don't know how to proceed Your PR hasn't been reviewed within the expected timeframe You need information or resources that aren't available What to Do When Blocked 1. Check the Policy First, review the relevant policies: Response times Code review guidelines This blocking issues policy Understanding the expectations can help you determine if your issue is truly blocking. 2. Communicate Clearly If you're blocked, communicate clearly and specifically: Good: "I submitted PR #123 on March 1st. It hasn't been reviewed yet. The stated response time is 48 hours. Can someone please review?" Not as helpful: "My PR has been sitting for weeks. This is ridiculous." 3. Provide Context Help others understand why you're blocked: What are you trying to accomplish? What have you tried so far? What specific information or action do you need? Why is this blocking your progress? 4. Escalate Appropriately If you've communicated and still haven't received a response within a reasonable time, you can: Ping in the issue/PR: A polite reminder can help Ask for a different reviewer: If one maintainer is unavailable, another might help Open a discussion: If the issue is about project direction rather than a specific PR Contact another maintainer: If your primary contact isn't responding, try someone else 5. Consider Alternatives If you're truly blocked and can't get a response, consider: Working around the blocker: Can you proceed without the blocked aspect? Posting your work: Share your work-in-progress to get feedback from the community Forking: If the project isn't responsive, you can fork and continue independently Finding another project: If this project isn't meeting your needs, another might be a better fit How Maintainers Should Handle Blocking Issues Respond Promptly When you see a contributor is blocked: Acknowledge quickly: "I see this is blocking you. Let me look into it." Provide information: Share what you know Make a decision: If you can't decide, say so and explain why Follow up: If you said you'd get back to someone, do so Provide Clear Guidance When a contributor is unsure about direction: Explain the reasoning behind decisions Point to relevant documentation Offer alternatives when possible Be honest about uncertainties Handle Conflicts When there's conflicting feedback: Acknowledge the conflict Explain the trade-offs Make a decision or facilitate a decision Document the decision for future reference Response Time Expectations Issue Type Expected Response Action If Exceeded Bug reports 48 hours Ping maintainers, if no response in 1 week, escalate Feature requests 1 week Ping maintainers, if no response in 2 weeks, open a discussion PRs 48 hours Ping maintainers, if no response in 1 week, ask for a different reviewer Questions 1 week Search docs first, then ask in discussion These are targets, not guarantees. If missed, communicate and adjust expectations. When to Escalate Escalate when: You've waited longer than the expected response time Your work is truly blocked and can't proceed You've received conflicting guidance and can't resolve it You feel ignored or dismissed How to escalate: Politely ping: "Hi, I'm still waiting on this. Can someone please help?" Tag other maintainers: If your primary contact is unavailable Open a discussion: For broader issues Contact the maintainer community: For serious concerns Community Support Contributors can also get support from: Other contributors: They may have experienced similar issues Discussion forums: Ask the community for advice Maintainer community: External support from other open source maintainers No Response If you've tried everything and still haven't received a response: Give it time: Sometimes maintainers are genuinely busy Try a different approach: Different communication channel, different language Accept the situation: The project may not be responsive Move on: There are many other projects that would welcome your contribution Remember: A project's responsiveness is a reflection of its maintainership, not your worth as a contributor. Last updated: 2026-09-04

docs.text: Setting Boundaries for Open Source Maintainers This guide helps maintainers establish and maintain healthy boundaries. ---Thank you to all the maintainers who shared their insights for this guide! Why Boundaries Matter Boundaries are the foundation of sustainable open source work. They protect your time, energy, and well-being while setting clear expectations for your community. Without boundaries, you risk: - Burnout from overcommitting - Resentment from unmet expectations - Loss of work-life balance - Diminished enjoyment of the work With boundaries, you create: - Predictability for yourself and others - Space for focused, meaningful work - Protection against scope creep and unreasonable demands - Permission to prioritize your well-being Types of Boundaries 1. Time Boundaries What they cover: When you work, how long, and how often. Examples: - "I work on Surypus weekdays from 9am to 5pm EST." - "I don't work on weekends." - "I take one week off per quarter." How to set them: 1. Decide your available hours 2. Communicate them clearly 3. Stick to them consistently 4. Update if your situation changes Template: "I am available to work on Surypus on [days] from [time] to [time] [timezone]. I don't work weekends. I will try to respond to issues within [timeframe]." 2. Scope Boundaries What they cover: What types of work you accept and what you decline. Examples: - "I don't review PRs that change the public API without prior discussion." - "I won't work on feature requests without an approved issue." - "I focus on core functionality, not plugins or integrations." How to set them: 1. Define your scope clearly 2. Document it in CONTRIBUTING or a dedicated document 3. Politely decline out-of-scope requests with explanation 4. Offer alternatives when possible Template: "Thanks for the suggestion! This is outside the scope of Surypus. The project focuses on [scope]. You might want to [alternative suggestion] or consider [alternative project]." 3. Communication Boundaries What they cover: How you communicate, through which channels, and with what response expectations. Examples: - "I respond to issues within 48 hours on weekdays." - "I don't check email evenings or weekends." - "I prefer discussing technical decisions in issues, not DMs." How to set them: 1. State your communication preferences clearly 2. Use templates for common responses 3. Set up auto-responders for breaks 4. Mute notifications outside work hours 5. Redirect private conversations to public channels Template: "I check issues weekly and respond within 48 hours on weekdays. For urgent matters, please cc [backup maintainer]. I prefer discussing technical decisions in public issues so others can learn." 4. Emotional Boundaries What they cover: How you handle criticism, conflict, and emotional demands. Examples: - "I don't read every comment on every issue." - "I separate feedback on my code from feedback on me as a person." - "I don't feel responsible for fixing every user's problem." How to set them: 1. Recognize emotional triggers 2. Develop healthy responses to criticism 3. Take breaks when emotions run high 4. Seek support from other maintainers 5. Remember: you're not responsible for everyone's happiness Common Boundary Challenges "But it's open source—I should be available!" Response: Open source doesn't mean unlimited availability. You choose your level of involvement. Many successful maintainers have clear boundaries. "Users will be upset if I say no." Response: Clear boundaries actually reduce frustration. Users may be temporarily disappointed, but consistent boundaries build trust over time. "I feel guilty saying no." Response: Guilt is common but not a reliable guide. Remind yourself: saying no to one thing means saying yes to your well-being and the things that matter most. "I'm afraid of losing contributors." Response: Clear boundaries often attract better contributors—those who respect your time and share your values. Templates for Common Scenarios Declining a Feature Request "Thanks for the suggestion! This is outside the scope of Surypus, which focuses on [scope]. This might be better suited for [alternative project] or a plugin. If you'd like to explore this further, please open an issue to discuss." Responding to Urgent Requests "I understand this is urgent for you. I'm not available evenings/weekends, but [backup maintainer] might be able to help. Otherwise, I'll look at this during my next available time on [day/time]." Handling Unreasonable Demands "I'm not able to [demand]. This is outside the scope of my involvement with Surypus. If you'd like to contribute this yourself, I'm happy to review your PR." Taking a Break "I'm taking a break from Surypus maintenance from [start date] to [end date]. I won't be responding to issues or PRs during this time. [Backup maintainer] may be able to help with urgent matters. Thank you for your understanding!" A Note on Saying No Saying "no" is a skill. It gets easier with practice. Why saying no is okay: - You have limited time and energy - Not every request deserves a yes - Saying no protects your ability to say yes to what matters - Clear "no"s are kinder than vague deferrals How to say no well: 1. Be direct and clear 2. Explain briefly (no over-apologizing) 3. Offer alternatives when possible 4. Do it kindly but firmly Remember: "No" is a complete sentence. You don't owe lengthy explanations. Maintaining Your Boundaries Setting boundaries is one thing. Keeping them is another. Tips for sticking to boundaries: - Automate reminders: Use calendar alerts for breaks - Use templates: Save pre-written responses for common scenarios - Find accountability: Check in with another maintainer about boundary adherence - Review regularly: Are your boundaries still working? Adjust as needed. Conclusion Boundaries aren't barriers—they're guardrails that let you sustainably contribute to open source. They protect your time, energy, and well-being while setting clear expectations for your community. Start small. Pick one boundary to set this week. Notice how it feels. Adjust as needed. You deserve to enjoy your open source work without burning out. Inspired by the experiences of many maintainers. docs.text: REST_POLICY.md This document describes the rest and break policy for Surypus maintainers. ---Inspired by maintainer communities worldwide. Thank you to everyone who shared their experiences. Why Rest Matters in Open Source Open source maintainership is sustainable only when maintainers practice self-care. This includes taking regular breaks from the project. This policy establishes: - Normal and expected break patterns - How to communicate breaks to the community - How the project continues during breaks - How to return from breaks This policy applies to: - All current and future maintainers - All types of maintenance work (issues, PRs, releases, etc.) - Both planned and unplanned breaks Normal Break Patterns Weekly Breaks Standard: Maintainers are expected to take at least one full day off per week from Surypus work. Recommended: Take weekends off, or choose one weekday as your break day. Communication: You don't need to announce weekly breaks. Just don't work on your break day. Monthly Breaks Standard: Maintainers are encouraged to take one longer break per month (3-7 days). Recommended: Schedule a quarterly long weekend or week off. Communication: Post in a GitHub issue or discussion 1-2 weeks before a longer break. Template: I'm planning to take a break from Surypus maintenance from [date] to [date]. I won't be reviewing PRs or responding to issues during this time. [Backup maintainer] can help with urgent matters. I'll be back on [return date]. Quarterly Breaks Standard: Maintainers are encouraged to take at least one week off per quarter (4 weeks per year). Recommended: Schedule one week of reduced activity or full break each quarter. Communication: Post 2-4 weeks before the break. Annual Breaks Standard: Maintainers are expected to take at least 2 weeks off per year. Recommended: Take a full vacation or sabbatical each year. Communication: Post 4-6 weeks before a long break. Planned Breaks How to Request a Planned Break Decide: Determine the dates and scope of your break Communicate: Post in the maintainer discussion or issue Delegate: Identify tasks that need coverage and who can handle them Update Status: Set your GitHub status to "On vacation" or similar Go: Take your break without guilt! Break Request Template ## Planned Break Request **Maintainer:** [your name] **Dates:** [start date] to [end date] **Scope:** [full break / reduced activity / no reviews / etc.] **Coverage Plan:** - [ ] Issues: [who will triage?] - [ ] PRs: [who will review?] - [ ] Releases: [who will handle?] - [ ] Other: [any other needs] **Notes:** [Any additional context] During Your Break Actually step away from the project Don't feel guilty about not working Trust your coverage plan Check in only if you want to Returning from a Break Catch up gradually: Start with small tasks Reconnect: Read recent discussions and catch up on context Reflect: Did the break help? What would you change next time? Resume normal work: Return to your regular maintenance rhythm Unplanned Breaks Sometimes you need a break unexpectedly—due to illness, personal emergencies, burnout, or simply needing space. Short Unplanned Breaks (1-3 days) No need to announce unless it's an emergency Set your GitHub status if you're not responding Resume when you're able Medium Unplanned Breaks (1-2 weeks) Post briefly if you're able: "I need to step away for a bit. I'll be back around [date]." If you have backup maintainers, let them know Set your GitHub status Long Unplanned Breaks (2+ weeks) Post what you can: "I need to take an extended break. I'll be back when I can. Thank you for understanding." If possible, ask a backup maintainer to cover urgent matters Set your GitHub status Mental Health Days Taking a day off for mental health is valid and encouraged. You don't need to explain or justify it. Take the day Set your status if you want Return when you're ready Coverage During Breaks Who Covers What? Task Primary Cover Backup Issue triage [Name] [Name] PR reviews [Name] [Name] Releases [Name] [Name] Community questions [Name] [Name] Security issues [Name] [Name] Coverage Request Template ## Coverage Request **Task:** [what needs coverage] **Timeframe:** [dates] **Urgency:** [normal / urgent / emergency] **Context:** [Any relevant details] **Preferred Coverage:** [Any preferences for who handles this] Burnout Prevention Signs You Need a Break Feeling drained or exhausted by the project Dreading opening issues or PRs Feeling resentful toward contributors or users Having trouble focusing or making decisions Physical symptoms (headaches, sleep problems, etc.) Withdrawing from the community What to Do Acknowledge: Recognize that you're burning out Take a break: Step away from the project Seek support: Talk to other maintainers or a professional Consider changes: What would make this sustainable long-term? Returning After Burnout Be patient with yourself Start small Consider what changes would help prevent burnout in the future It's okay to step back further if needed Encouraging a Healthy Culture This policy exists to normalize rest and self-care in the Surypus community. We expect: - Maintainers take breaks - Maintainers support each other's breaks - Contributors understand and respect break policies - No guilt trips or pressure to work during breaks We discourage: - Guilt-tripping maintainers for taking breaks - Expecting 24/7 availability - Punishing maintainers for taking time off - Creating urgency that prevents breaks Questions? If you have questions about this policy or need support taking a break, reach out to: - Other maintainers - The Surypus community in discussions - The maintainer community at Maintainer Community Last updated: 2026-09-04

docs.text: Self Care for Open Source Maintainers Maintaining an open source project is rewarding, but it can also be demanding. This guide offers practical advice for taking care of yourself while doing meaningful work. Why Self Care Matters Open source maintainership can be rewarding, but it also comes with unique challenges. Maintainers often face: Constant pressure to respond to issues and pull requests Unrealistic expectations from users and sponsors Isolation and loneliness Time management challenges Burnout from overcommitting Your well-being as a maintainer is essential. When you're healthy and balanced, you can better serve your community. Understanding Your Motivation Why do you do open source work? Knowing your "why" helps you stay motivated and make better decisions. Exercise: Write down your top 5 motivations for maintaining Surypus. Common motivations include: Helping others solve problems Learning new skills Building reputation and career Working on something you care about Making a positive impact on the world Connecting with a community Your motivations will evolve over time. Revisit this list periodically. Recognizing Burnout Signs Burnout is common among open source maintainers. Watch for these warning signs: Category Signs Emotional Feeling drained, cynical, or detached Physical Exhaustion, headaches, sleep problems Cognitive Can't focus, forget details, reduced productivity Behavioral Avoiding work, procrastinating, withdrawing Relational Irritable, impatient, less empathetic Self-Assessment: Rate these statements on a scale of 1-5 (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree): I feel exhausted at the thought of working on the project. [___] I've become more cynical about the project or users. [___] I've lost interest in work I used to enjoy. [___] I feel like nothing I do makes a difference. [___] I'm avoiding the project or putting it off. [___] My sleep or health has been affected. [___] I feel overwhelmed by the workload. [___] Score: ____ / 35 14-21: Some burnout risk. Take action soon. 22-28: Moderate burnout. Make significant changes. 29-35: High burnout risk. Consider stepping back. Strategies for Sustaining Your Energy Set Boundaries What boundaries do you need? Write down your boundaries: Time: I work on Surypus on [days] from [time] to [time]. Scope: I will not work on [types of contributions] because... Communication: I respond to issues within [timeframe]. Availability: I am unavailable on [dates/days]. Exercise: Draft your boundary statement. "I am available to work on Surypus on weekdays from 9am to 5pm EST. I will respond to issues within 48 hours. I am taking a break from reviewing PRs on weekends." Why boundaries matter: They protect your time and energy They set clear expectations for others They help you avoid overcommitting They model healthy behavior for the community Remember: Saying "no" is okay. You don't owe anyone your time. Take Breaks Schedule regular breaks: Daily breaks (e.g., 15 minutes every 2 hours) Weekly breaks (e.g., no open source on weekends) Vacation breaks (e.g., one week off per quarter) Sabbatical breaks (e.g., one month off per year) How to take a break effectively: Plan ahead - Tell your community in advance Update your status - Set your GitHub status and auto-responder Delegate tasks - Assign someone to handle urgent matters Disconnect - Actually step away from the project Return gradually - Start with small tasks when you come back Protect your sleep, exercise, and social connections. These are foundational to your well-being. Build a Support Network Who can you lean on? Other maintainers - Share experiences and advice Friends and family - Talk about your fears and frustrations Community members - Appreciate their support and feedback Professional help - Consider therapy or counseling if needed Join communities like: Maintainer Community Open Source Mental Health Local meetups and user groups Celebrate Successes It's easy to focus on what's broken. Make time to recognize what's working. Celebrate: 🎉 First-time contributors ⭐ New milestones (stars, downloads, adopters) 🐛 Bugs fixed 📖 Documentation improved 🤝 Community connections made Keep a victory log. Write down 3 things you're proud of each week. Practice Self-Compassion Maintaining open source is hard. Be kind to yourself. Forgive yourself for mistakes and imperfections Accept your limits - You can't do everything Focus on impact - What you do matters, even if it's not perfect Ask for help - It's okay to need support Resources The Maintainer's Corner Burnout Checklist Open Source Mental Health SustainOSS Rockwood Leadership Institute Saying No, Mike McQuaid Check-In Questions Ask yourself regularly: Am I enjoying my work on this project? Am I energized or drained after working on it? Am I meeting my own needs (sleep, health, relationships)? Am I setting and keeping boundaries? Do I have support when I need it? If you're struggling, reach out. You're not alone. This guide is inspired by the work of many maintainers. Thank you to everyone who shared their experiences.

docs.text: Maintainer Sustainability Guide Practical strategies for sustainable open source maintainership. ---Thank you to all the maintainers who shared their wisdom for this guide! The Sustainability Challenge Open source maintainership is often seen as a labor of love, but sustaining it long-term requires more than enthusiasm. It requires: Realistic expectations about time and energy Systems that reduce repetitive work Community support structures Clear boundaries and communication Financial sustainability (when possible) This guide covers practical strategies for each area. Realistic Expectations Time How much time do you actually have? Be honest with yourself. Consider: Your day job and other commitments Family and personal time Health and energy levels Other open source projects Exercise: Track your time for one week. How much did you spend on Surypus? Was it sustainable? Common patterns: - Many maintainers spend 5-10 hours/week on their projects - Some work in bursts (sprint then rest) - Some have regular weekly time blocks There's no "right" amount. Find what works for you. Energy What drains you? What energizes you? Draining Activities Energizing Activities Reviewing large PRs Helping new contributors Dealing with conflicts Writing documentation Responding to unfair criticism Learning new things Context switching Deep work on features Strategy: Structure your work to maximize energizing activities and minimize draining ones. Automation Strategies Automate repetitive tasks to free up time for meaningful work. What to Automate Task Tool/Approach Welcome new contributors welcome-contributors.yml Stale issue management stale.yml Label issues/PRs labeler.yml Auto-merge dependencies auto-merge-deps.yml CI/CD runs GitHub Actions workflows Release notes release-drafter.yml Security scanning CodeQL, Secret scanning What NOT to Automate Code review (personal judgment needed) Community interactions (authenticity matters) Strategic decisions (human judgment essential) Conflict resolution (empathy required) GitHub Actions for Maintainer Support Consider these additional automations: Reminder bots - Gently remind about stale PRs Assignment bots - Auto-assign issues to willing contributors Thank-you bots - Celebrate milestones Status updates - Auto-post about your availability Support Structures Delegate to Contributors Your contributors are your best resource. Use them. Delegation opportunities: - Triaging issues (labeling, closing duplicates) - Reviewing straightforward PRs - Writing documentation - Answering questions in discussions - Organizing community events - Creating tutorials and examples How to delegate effectively: 1. Identify tasks you can hand off 2. Find contributors interested in those tasks 3. Give clear expectations and guidelines 4. Trust them to do the work 5. Provide feedback and recognition Build a Team You don't have to maintain a project alone. Team structures: - Co-maintainers - Shared ownership, similar responsibilities - Maintainers for areas - Different people own different modules - Advisory board - Guidance without direct maintenance work - Community managers - Handle community interactions How to recruit team members: - Look for consistent, helpful contributors - Ask them directly if they'd be interested - Offer clear roles and expectations - Start with small responsibilities and grow Seek External Support Resources: - Maintainer Community - Connect with other maintainers - SustainOSS - Funding and sustainability resources - Open Source Collective - Fiscal sponsorship - GitHub Sponsors - Direct funding Types of support: - Emotional support (talking with other maintainers) - Technical support (collaborators who help with work) - Financial support (sponsors, grants, paid contracts) - Legal support (advice on licensing, trademarks) Communication Strategies Responsive But Not Instant You don't need to respond immediately to everything. Reasonable response times: - Bug reports: 48 hours - Feature requests: 1 week - PRs: 48 hours - General questions: 1 week If you can't meet these times, that's okay. Set expectations clearly and communicate delays. Deflecting Private Messages Private messages lead to burnout. Public channels are better for the community. Politely redirect: "Hey! Could you please ask this in a GitHub issue? It'll help others who have the same question, and I'll be able to respond more thoughtfully." Setting Response Expectations In your README or CONTRIBUTING: "I try to respond to issues within 48 hours on weekdays. I don't work weekends. For urgent matters, please cc [backup maintainer]." During breaks: "I'm on vacation until [date]. I won't be responding to issues or PRs during this time." Handling Unreasonable Expectations Some people will make demands that aren't reasonable. That's okay. You can politely decline. "I understand this is important to you, but I'm not able to [request]. This is outside the scope of my involvement with the project. If you'd like to work on this yourself, I'm happy to review your contribution." Be transparent: - Share how funds are used - Report on progress and impact - Thank sponsors publicly (with permission) Taking Breaks Why Breaks Matter Breaks prevent burnout and improve the quality of your work. docs.text: Open source maintainership is often seen as a labor of love, but sustaining it long-term requires more than enthusiasm. It requires: Realistic expectations about time and energy Systems that reduce repetitive work Community support structures Clear boundaries and communication Financial sustainability (when possible) This guide covers practical strategies for each area.

docs.text: How much time do you actually have? Be honest with yourself. Consider: Your day job and other commitments Family and personal time Health and energy levels Other open source projects Exercise: Track your time for one week. How much did you spend on Surypus? Was it sustainable? Common patterns: - Many maintainers spend 5-10 hours/week on their projects - Some work in bursts (sprint then rest) - Some have regular weekly time blocks There's no "right" amount. Find what works for you.
